caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1098 of 2023
lawyer:
Mr. Golam Mostqfa, Advocate instructed by Mrs. Madhu Malati Chowdhuiy Barua, Advocate-on-Record. ------ For the Petitioner 
Mr Md. Ataur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, Rohanpur Branch, Rohanpur, Chapai-Nawabganj. ------- Opposite party no.2-Petitioner.
Vs.
Md. Jewel Islam and another. --------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Md. Shahinur Islam J. This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 08.12.2022 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 42086 of 2021 making the Rule absolute arising out of the Sessions Case No.650 of 2018 Corresponding to C.R. Case No.126 of 2018 (Gomostapur) under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (hereinafter) referred to as 'the Act, 1881') now pending before the learned Joint Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Chapai Nawabganj. 

 2. Facts relevant for disposal of the instant petition are that the petitioner, Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, Rohanpur Branch, Rohanpur, Chapai-Nawabganj, as complainant filed C. R. Case No. 126 of 2018 (Gomostapur) in the Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chapai Nawabganj, under Section 138 of the Act, 1881, alleging inter-alia, that the accused, Md. Jewel Islam as customer, has borrowed investment from the petitioner bank and in return of which the accused issued a cheque bearing No.9153282 on 20.02.2018 with a face-value of Tk. 35,83,700.00/- (Thirty five lac eighty three thousand and seven hundred taka), to be drawn from Al-Wadiyah Current Account No-783, maintained with the complainant bank and the said cheque was presented for encashment on the very same day but the said cheque was dishonored due to insufficient fund. Thereafter, the complainant issued legal notice on 25.02.2018 upon the accused for payment of the money within a period of 30 (thirty) days but the accused-petitioner failed to pay the money within the stipulated time as mentioned in the legal notice. Thus, the complainant filed the aforesaid C.R. case under section 138 of the Act, 1881. 

 3. Learned Magistrate after examining the complainant under Section 200 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Code, 1898') took cognizance of offence under Section 13 of the Act, 1881 against the accused. Thereafter, the accused person was enlarged on bail and the case was transferred to the Court of learned Sessions Judge, Chapai Nawabganj for trial wherein the case was registered as Sessions Case No.650 of 2018. 

 4. Subsequently the case record was transferred to the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Chapai Nawabganj for trial and disposal of the case. 

 7. Eventually, the case record was transferred to the learned Joint Sessions Judge, 1st Court, Chapai Nawabganj for trial and disposal which is still pending before said Court. 

 8. Thereafter, the accused-respondent no.1, as petitioner preferred Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.42086 of 2021 under Section 561A of the Code, 1898, for quashing the proceeding of the Sessions Case No. 650 of 2018. 

 9. After contested hearing a Division Bench of the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and thereby quashed the proceeding of the Sessions Case No. 650 of 2018 vide judgment and order dated 08A 2.2022, upon a finding that: 

 "We have carefully gone through the provision of Sections 141, 7 and 9 of the Negotiable Instrument- Act, 1881 and we hold that in order to take cognizance of a case under Section 138 of the above Act the complaint must be submitted by the payee or holder in due course of the cheque. 

 We further hold that above mentioned payee or holder in due course must be a person, natural or juristic.' In the instant case it turns out from the record that the impugned cheque was not issued in favour of a person natural or juristic. It was issued against an account number which does not fall in the category of per-son as mentioned above. Hence the impugned cheque was not issued in favour of a person and the complaint of this case was not filed by the payee or holder in due course of above cheque. The learned Joint Sessions Judge committed serious illegality in framing charge against the petitioner and proceeding with the useless and futile trial of the case. Above trial will not bring any fruitful result for the complainant nor the same will satisfi, the cause of justice, but the same will result into unnecessary suffering and plight of the petitioner. Above proceedings is a still born and unnecessary one which deserves to be quashed" 

 11. Mr. Golam Mostafa, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the High Court Division without considering the facts and circumstances of this case that the respondent no.1 took loan from the complainant bank and issued the cheque in question for paying installment of loan and after observing all the legal formalities the complainant filed the case wherein charge was framed and evidence of P.W 1 was recorded and the case is still pending for final adjudication and at this stage in no way the criminal proceeding would be quashed , as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set-aside. 

 15. The core question involved in this criminal petition is that whether the complainant is precluded from filing the case as the alleged cheque did not contain the name of the complainant as payee or holder in due course. 16. To adjudicate the dispute involved in this criminal petition we need to discuss section 141 (a) of the Act, 1881, which mandates that no court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under section 138 except upon a complaint, in writing, made by the payee or, as the case may be, the holder in due course of the cheque. 

 17. So section 141(a) of the Act, 1881, provides that except with the written complainant made by the "payee" or the "holder in due course" of the cheque, no court shall take cognizance of the offence punishable under section 138 of the Act, 1881. However, it should kept in mind that the facts and circumstances of all cases are not similar and everyone should be given an opportunity to establish his/her claim by adducing proper evidence except where there is an express bar. Again, the rule of principles of natural justice is that the parties should be given a fair opportunity to be heard so that no one can be prejudiced. 

 19. Furthermore, it also apparent from the record that the respondent no. 1 wrote the name of the payee of the cheque as "Mura-1252" with his own hand writing and issued the same as part payment of the loan amount. Thus, there might be a relation of this case with the writing "Mura-1252". 

 20. It is pertinent to mention here that the trial of the case has been started and deposition of P.W. 1 has also been recorded by the trial court and the case is remaining for the cross-examination of P.W. 1 by the accused person. In this view of matter since the trial of the case has already been started and the P.W. 1 has been examined as such the question raised by the respondent no. 1 can be settled by the trial court after examining the evidence on record. Moreover, if the case is quashed before conclusion of the trial then the complainant would lose the opportunity to prove his/her claim and in such a situation the complainant becomes non-suited, which is not desirable. 

 21. Apart from this, it transpires from the record that the accused-respondent no. 1 took loan from the complainant bank i.e. the Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, Rohanpur Branch, Rohanpur, Chapai-Nawabganj and for the purpose of payment of loan money, the accused-respondent no. 1 gave the cheque in question on 20.02.2018 to the complainant which was dishonored on the same date due to insufficient fund in his bank account. It also transpires from the record that pursuant to the provision of section 138 (1) (b) of the Act, 1881, the complainant issued a legal notice on 25.02.2018 upon the accused-respondent no. 1. Thereafter, the complainant filed the case on 11.04.2018 before the competent court concerned. Thus, prima facie it appears that the complaint petition was filed within the time-frame as stipulated in the Act, 1881. 

 22. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the discussions made herein above, we are of the view that since the fact of taking loan from the complainant bank as well as issuance of alleged cheque is not disputed and "Mura-1252" is the account number of the accused-respondent no.1 which is maintained by the complainant bank through which payment of the loan money is regulated and the trial of the case has already been started, the question raised by the accused person-respondent no.1 can be well settled by the trial court after examining the evidence on record. 

 25. The impugned judgment and order dated 08.12.2022, passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 42086 of 2021, is hereby set-aside.
